item.title: Six Shadertoy shaders, read line by line
item.description:
Between January and February 2024 I published six shaders on Shadertoy[1]. Some are my own experiments, and some start from well-known shaders that I modified to learn how they work. This post reads each one line by line: what the code computes, where the ideas come from, and where the code does something other than what its comments say.

Each embed starts paused, so the page does not run six shaders at once. Press play to run one.

item.title: TrueMapData: from measured height maps to usable assets
item.description: TrueMapData reads surface captures from TrueMap and GelSight, exposes their heights as NumPy arrays, and provides tools for analysis and graphics export. The same surface representation supports metrology work and assets such as displacement maps or meshes.

item.title: Dimension: connecting Rust mathematics to a renderer
item.description: Dimension is my Rust workspace for mathematics and graphics experiments. The useful starting point is mathlib: it exposes matrix storage, numerical solvers and the transformations that the rendering crate uses on the CPU.

item.title: Artemis Switch: following a frame from the network to the screen
item.description:
antoinebou12/Artemis-Switch

★ 36 · 2 forks · Repository created 2026-08-08

GitHub statistics recorded 2026-11-05.

A stream can report a healthy bitrate and still feel late. Artemis Switch is my Moonlight-Switch fork for Nintendo Switch, focused on the path between receiving a frame and presenting it. The useful question is not just “how fast is the decoder?” but “where did this frame wait?”

item.title: Porting sm64coopdx to Switch and New 3DS: keep the platform boundary small
item.description:
antoinebou12/sm64coopdx-switch-N3DS

★ 4 · 1 forks · Repository created 2026-08-19

GitHub statistics recorded 2026-11-05.

The interesting part of a console port is rarely a single compiler flag. sm64coopdx-switch-N3DS brings the Coop Deluxe engine to two very different handheld targets. The work lives at the platform boundary: graphics, input, audio, threading, and packaging.

This fork builds on the Coop Deluxe Team’s sm64coopdx, which continues djoslin0’s sm64ex-coop. The multiplayer engine and Lua ecosystem are upstream work; the console adapters are the focus here.
